messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT 3102 — High tail latency observed for /v1/generate (p99 > 4000ms) across us-west-2 region. Pager routed to Ashley (oncall).

Ashley (oncall): acked, looking. I've seen a couple of spikes on dashboard. Investigating request queue and model fallback logs.

Ashley (oncall): quick check — are we seeing increased batch sizes or a model fallback loop?

Sara (sre): I'm seeing a burst of long requests from a single customer IP range, and KV cache miss rate for recent prefixes jumped. Possible cold-KV churn.

Mike (infra): scaling a few replicas now (autoscaler didn't catch the sudden RPS because of short spike). Pushing +2 replicas to the nodepool in us-west-2.

deploy-bot: Triggered rollout: scale replicas +2 for service redwood-inference/generation-usw2 at 1718204698 by mike_infra.

Lee (metrics): posting quick metrics: p50=300ms, p95=1200ms, p99=4200ms, error rate 0.8%. GPU util at 92% on primary pool. Queue depth up to 48. Cache hit rate down from 83% to 58% in last 15m.

Ashley (oncall): mitigation: temporarily route heavy customers to a lower-latency model variant (redwood-llama-7b-q4f) as fallback policy. Applying routing override for affected customer prefixes.

Ashley (oncall): set routing override -> command: `rbctl route override --prefix 203.0.113.0/24 --model redwood-llama-7b-q4f --ttl 30m`

Sara (sre): confirmed fallback routing in logs. tailing `inference-router.log` shows requests being remapped. Early signs of p99 drop for that prefix.

Lee (metrics): after fallback, p99 for affected prefix dropped to ~1100ms, overall p99 to 1500ms. GPU util down to 78%. Queue depth trending down.

Jordan (product): any customer impact outbound? Should we notify CS if we expect degradation for a subset?

Ashley (oncall): short note to CS: "We've routed heavy traffic to a compatible model variant to reduce latency; quality for those requests may differ. We're continuing to investigate and will follow up in the incident retro."

Mike (infra): follow-up: autoscaler config looks like it uses 5m CPU smoothing which missed the 2m spike. We should tune scaling window or add a queue-depth-based autoscaling metric.

Sara (sre): agreed. Also the alert that fired is p99 > 3000ms over 5m. That rule generated a lot of noise in the past; it fired three times in the last 24h where tech team chased blips. We need an improved alerting strategy postmortem.

Ashley (oncall): leaving a TODO in the thread: 1) Assess alert noise, 2) Tune thresholds/durations, 3) Build a Grafana retro dashboard with drilldowns and golden signals, 4) Add runbook links to alerts. Assigning owners below.

Lee (metrics): sketching the dashboard panels we should add for the retro (will create Grafana dashboard JSON in infra repo):
- Golden signals row: p50/p95/p99 latency, request rate, error rate, saturation (GPU util), queue depth.
- Top-k routes by p99 and by request volume (table + heatmap).
- Cache metrics: KV cache hit ratio, KV eviction rate, prefix churn.
- Autoscaler observability: scaling events timeline, scaling lag (time from threshold breach to replicas active).
- Fallbacks: count of routed-to-fallback events per prefix, model variant switch timeline.
- Alert timeline: which alert rules fired, grouped by severity, with links to alert definitions.
- Drilldown panels: a panel that links a p99 spike to traces (Tempo) and to recent deploys (deploy-bot events).

Lee (metrics): example PromQL for p99 panel: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{route=~"/v1/generate.*"}[5m])) by (le))`

Mike (infra): also add a panel for batch sizes and queue depth relation. PromQL: `sum by (instance) (rate(inference_batch_size_sum[1m])) / sum by (instance) (rate(inference_batch_size_count[1m]))` for avg batch size.

Sara (sre): on alerts: proposals — reduce noise by using two-stage firing: 1) p99 > 3000ms over 2m opens a WARNING; 2) if sustained for 10m or accompanied by queue_depth > 30 or gpu_util > 85% escalate to PAGE. That should prevent short blips from paging. Also add a grouped alert that suppresses duplicates from same customer prefix within 15m.

Ashley (oncall): love the two-stage idea. We should add enrichment to the alert payload: include `top_prefix`, `recent_deploy_id`, `fallback_count` and a link to the retro Grafana panel. Alerts that include runbook link: generate one-liner runbook to route/pin model, scale, and notify CS.

Jordan (product): curious — can we flag customer-impacting events automatically? e.g., if fallback_count > 0 for a paid tenant AND error_rate > 0.5% for that tenant then include "customer-impact: true" in the alert payload so CS gets a prepopulated message.

Mike (infra): we can add tenant tags in the router logs and expose `requests_by_tenant` metric. Then alerting rules can `sum by (tenant) (...)`. Will need to watch privacy/PII but we only store tenant-id.

Sara (sre): dashboard drilldowns: clicking on a p99 spike should open a panel variable `?prefix=203.0.113.0/24` and show traces filtered by that prefix. Also include a panel to view recent config changes: deploys, routing override events, autoscaler config changes.

Lee (metrics): I'll draft the Grafana dashboard JSON with panels: each panel will include a field `links` with macros for `dashboard:tempo-traces?var-prefix=$prefix` and `dashboard:deploys?from=$__from&to=$__to`.

Ashley (oncall): action items (owners & due):
- Lee: create Grafana retro dashboard + initial panels (p99, top routes, cache, autoscaler) — due EOD tomorrow.
- Mike: add `queue_depth` to autoscaler decision matrix and reduce CPU smoothing window to 90s — due next week.
- Sara: update alert rules to two-stage and add suppression by prefix; add runbook links — due in 3 days.
- Jordan: prepare CS template for impacted tenants and decide notification policy — due in 2 days.

Mike (infra): note: will post a small infra PR for autoscaler changes and expose `requests_by_tenant` metric.

Lee (metrics): drafting panel queries now. I'll push to `infra/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/incident-retro-1718204523.json` and open a PR for review.

Sara (sre): for the alert suppression logic, use a dedupe window: `for: 10m` on the escalate rule and `labels: {dedupe_prefix: "{{ $labels.prefix }}"}` so pagerduty/opsgenie dedup will match.

Ashley (oncall): thanks all. Once Lee's dashboard PR lands, we'll point the incident postmortem to it and attach screenshots. Planning a 30m retro tomorrow 10:00 PT — calendar invite to follow.

Jordan (product): thanks team — happy path here. Keep CS looped.

deploy-bot: deploy completed: routing override applied (ttl 30m) at 1718204801.

Ashley (oncall): closing the immediate page — monitoring for 1h. We'll reopen if any regression. Leaving this thread as the canonical mitigation log. :white_check_mark: 

Sara (sre): leaving a short note for post-incident writeup: root cause hypothesis = cache churn from hot prefixes causing KV misses -> larger batch assembly time + autoscaler smoothing prevented quick scale -> tail latency spike. Next steps align with dashboard/alerting changes above.

Lee (metrics): saved draft dashboard and PR link will be posted in this thread when ready.

Mike (infra): +1. Good job and clean mitigation path.

Ashley (oncall): end of thread — thanks everyone.
